solar_power_forecasting.investigation_finding: Linear regression achieves lower MAE on this bundled dataset because the benchmark data was synthesized with an exact linear formula (power_mw = 0.0019 * irradiance_wm2) without noise. In real utility-scale plants, Random Forest is preferred to handle physical nonlinearities: inverter MPPT clipping, temperature derating coefficients, and diurnal inverter heat-loss curves.

wind_power_forecasting.investigation_finding: Linear regression achieves lower MAE on this bundled dataset because the dummy wind output was generated using an affine approximation (P ≈ 0.45 * v - 1.36). In actual wind turbines, power follows a nonlinear cubic curve (P ∝ v³) that saturates at rated speed and shuts down at cut-out, which requires nonlinear models such as Random Forest.
